replies.poison_human: Ring the Poisons Information line on {poison_number} now. It is free, open 24 hours, and they will tell you exactly what to do. Ring {emergency} straight away if the person is drowsy, hard to wake, struggling to breathe, fitting, or vomiting repeatedly. Do not make them vomit, and keep the packet or bottle to read out. If this is actually an animal, ring your vet or an emergency vet instead.
replies.poison_human_nolines: Ring your local poisons information line now, and ring {emergency} straight away if the person is drowsy, hard to wake, struggling to breathe, fitting, or vomiting repeatedly. Do not make them vomit, and keep the packet or bottle to read out. If this is actually an animal, ring your vet or an emergency vet instead.
replies.poison_animal: Ring your vet now, or the nearest emergency vet if it is after hours, and tell them what was eaten and roughly how much. Do not make them vomit unless the vet says to, and keep the packet to read out. If it turns out a person swallowed it, ring {emergency} instead.
replies.object_urgent: Ring {emergency} now. A swallowed button battery, magnet or sharp object can seriously injure the throat or gut within hours, even if the person seems well, so do not wait for symptoms. Do not give food or drink and do not make them vomit. The Poisons Information line on {poison_number} can advise while you get help, and keep the packaging or a matching one to show.
replies.object_urgent_nolines: Ring {emergency} now. A swallowed button battery, magnet or sharp object can seriously injure the throat or gut within hours, even if the person seems well, so do not wait for symptoms. Do not give food or drink and do not make them vomit. Your local poisons information line can advise while you get help, and keep the packaging or a matching one to show.
replies.object_signs: Ring {emergency} now. A swallowed object with drooling, pain, trouble swallowing or breathing, gagging or vomiting needs help straight away. Stay with them, keep them upright, do not give food or drink, and do not make them vomit.
replies.object_minor: Ring {emergency} now if there is choking, trouble breathing, drooling, pain, or they cannot swallow or keep anything down. If none of that is happening, ring the Poisons Information line on {poison_number} for advice, and keep a close watch for those signs, vomiting, belly pain or a fever over the next few days. See your GP or an emergency department if any appear or you are worried. Do not make them vomit.
replies.object_minor_nolines: Ring {emergency} now if there is choking, trouble breathing, drooling, pain, or they cannot swallow or keep anything down. If none of that is happening, ring your local poisons information line for advice, and keep a close watch for those signs, vomiting, belly pain or a fever over the next few days. See your GP or an emergency department if any appear or you are worried. Do not make them vomit.
replies.emergency_number: Ring {emergency}. It is free, answered 24 hours, and they will talk you through what to do until help arrives. Tell them where you are and what happened, and stay on the line.
replies.emergency_number_poison: For something swallowed or eaten you can also ring the Poisons Information line on {poison_number}, but ring {emergency} straight away if the person is unwell.
replies.emergency_number_poison_nolines: For something swallowed or eaten you can also ring your local poisons information line, but ring {emergency} straight away if the person is unwell.
replies.thread_back: Ask me again about the rest when you are ready and I will pick it straight back up.
replies.minor_prefix: Tell a grown-up near you right now.
replies.heart: Ring {emergency} now. Chest tightness, especially with an arm that tingles, can be a heart problem, so do not wait to see if it passes. Do not drive yourself; sit down, unlock the door, and have someone stay with you.
replies.stroke: Ring {emergency} now. Face drooping, slurred speech or sudden weakness can be a stroke, and minutes matter. Note the time it started.
replies.breathing: Ring {emergency} now. Trouble breathing or swelling in the throat needs help straight away; stay sitting upright.
replies.bleeding: Ring {emergency} now. Bleeding that will not stop, or blood coming up, needs help straight away; press firmly on any wound you can see.
replies.worst_headache: Ring {emergency} now. A sudden severe headache, or a headache with a stiff neck and fever, needs help straight away.
replies.vision: Blurred or changed vision, especially with a headache that has lasted days, is not something to wait on. Please see a doctor today: your GP, or the emergency department if you cannot get in. Ring {emergency} straight away if it suddenly gets worse, or you feel confused, weak on one side, have trouble speaking, or keep vomiting.
replies.blood_out: Blood where it should not be is worth getting checked today. Please see your GP, or the emergency department if you cannot get in. Ring {emergency} if there is a lot of it, or you feel faint or unwell.
replies.glucose_low: {value} {unit} is low. Have about 15 grams of fast sugar now, such as half a glass of juice or regular soft drink, then recheck in 15 minutes and repeat if it is still under {low_line}. Ring {emergency} if the person is confused, cannot swallow safely, or will not wake. Check your diabetes plan or your GP about why it dropped.
replies.glucose_ok: {value} {unit} is in the usual range for someone with diabetes ({usual}). Your own targets may differ, so check your plan or your GP.
replies.glucose_up: {value} {unit} is a little above the usual range for someone with diabetes ({usual}). It is not an emergency on its own. Drink some water, recheck later, and mention it to your GP or diabetes team if it keeps running high. Check your own plan for your targets.
replies.glucose_high: {value} {unit} is high. Drink water, take any medicine exactly as your plan says, and contact your GP or diabetes team today. Ring {emergency} if you are vomiting, breathing fast, very drowsy or confused.
replies.glucose_usual_mmol: about 4 to 7 mmol/L before eating, up to about 10 after meals
replies.glucose_usual_mg: about 72 to 126 mg/dL before eating, up to about 180 after meals
